newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: MOZAMBIQUE SAYS CATTLE NUMBERS TRIPLE.
newsitem.headline: MOZAMBIQUE SAYS CATTLE NUMBERS TRIPLE.

text.p: The number of cattle in Mozambique more than tripled between 1992 and 1996 as a result of government and donor efforts to rebuild the national livestock herd, agriculture minister Carlos do Rosario said on Thursday.
He said cattle numbers rose to 400,000 from 100,000 over the five-year period.
Rosario told reporters the government wanted the country to rely less on foreign aid to help with the restocking.
Mozambique lost thousands of cattle in the 1980s during the country's 16-year civil war when peasants fled to neighbouring countries taking their livestock with them.
Since a peace agreement in 1992 between the ruling Frelimo-led government and former Renamo rebels, refugees had returned with their animals.
Rosario said cattle rustling in the country was however a problem that was affecting the restocking programme.
He said in the southern Maputo province hundreds of cattle had been stolen and taken across the border to South Africa and Swaziland or slaughtered and sold as meat in informal markets in Mozambique.
The agriculture minister said the government was considering privatising state-owned livestock companies which had been abandoned since the war.
